description: Welcome to Space in a Vacuum, a dynamic multidisciplinary team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! We transform empty space into boundless potential by combining code, design, and scientific problem-solving. While our name nods to the cosmic void, our approach is filled with fresh ideas and collaborative energy. We specialize in breaking down complex Earth and space data to build intuitive, impactful applications. Driven by curiosity and rapid innovation, we turn blank slates into real-world solutions.
summary: SkyZoom is a free single-page web tool that works like Google Earth for the night sky. You zoom from the whole sky down to a small patch, type any RA/Dec, and watch how a target moves over time.SPHEREx maps the sky every 6 months in 102 infrared bands. Moving objects (asteroids, comets, brown dwarfs, nearby stars) are found by comparing images over time, but the data is huge and existing tools are hard for beginners.SkyZoom makes that method usable in seconds: a guided 4-step tour, progressive zoom, a coordinates box (degrees or h/m/s), a time slider with a dot for each 6-month visit, and a Blink mode that flashes two visits so movers pop out.Citizen scientists have found most known brown dwarfs and many comets this way. Making the method understandable lets far more people help.
details:
Title
SkyZoom – Zoom from the Whole Sky to One Moving Star

One-liner
A free Google Earth–style sky explorer that lets anyone zoom, jump to coordinates, and watch targets move across SPHEREx visit times.

What we built
A single-page web tool (~14 KB, no install, no login) where you:

  • Zoom from the whole sky → constellation → small patch
  • Fly to any RA/Dec (degrees or 08h55m10.8s)
  • Use 5 presets: Barnard’s Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi, RW Aur, R Dra
  • Play a time slider with dots for each ~6-month SPHEREx visit
  • Blink two visits so movers pop out
  • Follow a 4-step guided tour in plain language

Challenge it addresses
Planet X and SPHEREx — SPHEREx maps the whole sky every 6 months in 102 infrared bands. Moving objects are found by comparing images over time, but the data is huge and existing tools are hard for beginners.

How it solves it
Makes the “compare over time” method understandable in seconds with progressive zoom, a tour, coordinates, time animation, and Blink mode.

Why it matters
Citizen scientists have already found most known brown dwarfs and many comets this way. Lowering the barrier lets far more people help.

Tech
HTML + CSS + JavaScript (Canvas), stereographic projection, catalogue proper motion, GitHub Pages. Auto Low-end mode. Works offline after first load.

NASA data used

  • NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx mission & Level-2 docs → 6-month revisit design
  • NASA WiseView / Backyard Worlds → blink method
  • Challenge targets & WISE 0855 coordinate.

AI
Code, copy, and slides generated with Claude under team direction/review. Disclosed in README and submission. No AI images/video. No NASA logos.
